content: 1. Dosage and Administration: The safety and efficacy of cefepime/enmetazobactam have not been fully established. It is recommended to visually inspect the diluted solution for particulate matter and discoloration before administration. The solution should appear clear to yellowish. 2. Drug Interactions: BCG Vaccine (Live): Cefepime/enmetazobactam reduces the efficacy of the BCG intravesical live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic treatment. Cholera Vaccine: Systemic antibiotics, including cefepime/enmetazobactam, may inactivate the cholera vaccine strain. Avoid administering the vaccine to patients who have received antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): The efficacy of the typhoid vaccine is reduced by cefepime/enmetazobactam. Wait until antibiotic treatment is completed before administering the vaccine. Oral Microbiota: Cefepime/enmetazobactam may reduce the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (e.g., atezolizumab, avelumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab): Co-administration with cefepime/enmetazobactam may interfere with the therapeutic effects of these agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Hormonal Contraceptives (e.g., ethinyl estradiol, levonorgestrel): Cefepime/enmetazobactam may reduce the efficacy of oral hormonal contraceptives by altering intestinal flora. While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, consider using an additional or alternative form of birth control during concomitant use. Aminoglycosides (e.g., amikacin, gentamicin, tobramycin): Cefepime/enmetazobactam may increase the nephrotoxic and/or ototoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor renal function closely. Furosemide: Co-administration with potent diuretics like furosemide may increase nephrotoxicity. Monitor renal function closely. Probenecid: Probenecid increases the levels of cefepime/enmetazobactam by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Warfarin: Cefepime/enmetazobactam may increase the effects of warfarin and reduce prothrombin activity. Monitor coagulation parameters closely. 3. Adverse Effects: Common adverse effects include increased transaminases (20%), elevated bilirubin (7%), headache (5%), phlebitis or infusion site reactions (5%), diarrhea (4%), anemia (3%), and hypersensitivity reactions (2%). Less common effects include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and restlessness. Serious adverse effects include encephalopathy (e.g., altered consciousness, hallucinations, seizures), anaphylaxis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, hepatic dysfunction, renal dysfunction, and hemorrhage. 4. Special Populations: Pregnancy: There is limited data on the use of cefepime/enmetazobactam during pregnancy. Observational studies with cephalosporins, including cefepime, have not established an increased risk of major birth defects or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Breastfeeding: There is no information on the effects of cefepime/enmetazobactam on breastfed infants or milk production. 5. Precautions: Patients with a history of hypersensitivity to beta-lactam antibiotics, including cefepime, should avoid this medication. Monitor prothrombin time in patients at risk of reduced prothrombin activity (e.g., those with renal or hepatic impairment, poor nutritional status, or prolonged antibiotic use). Administer vitamin K as needed. Avoid prescribing antibiotics in the absence of a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection to reduce the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. 6. General Recommendations: Monitor renal and hepatic function during treatment, especially in patients with pre-existing conditions or those receiving nephrotoxic agents. Educate patients on the potential side effects and the importance of completing the prescribed antibiotic course. This information is intended for healthcare professionals to guide safe and effective use of cefepime/enmetazobactam. Always refer to the latest prescribing information for updates.
